classes.name: Loop diuretics
classes.description: Loop diuretics: furosemide (Lasix; tablets, oral solution; Furoscix subcutaneous on-body infusor and Lasix ONYU subcutaneous, alternatives only, never the pick), torsemide (generic; Soaanz), bumetanide (Bumex), ethacrynic acid (Edecrin; for sulfa allergy). Not thiazides.
classes.plainDescription: A strong water pill that removes extra fluid, for heart failure, kidney and liver disease and swelling.

preferredAgent.sig: Edema: 20 to 80 mg by mouth as a single dose; repeat or raise by 20 or 40 mg no sooner than 6 to 8 hours later until the response is right (label). Check potassium.
preferredAgent.plainSig: One pill in the morning. Your dose may be adjusted to how much fluid you lose.

alternatives.drug: Furosemide (oral solution, 10 mg/mL and 40 mg/5 mL)

records.verificationNote: Diuretic rows on PDF p.54 (printed p.38), section DIURETICS. Pick furosemide 20 mg tablet, Tier 2, no PA. Furoscix, Lasix ONYU and Soaanz have no row; recorded nonformulary under the closed-formulary statement. Edecrin is listed at Tier 5, no PA printed. [Sonnet check 2026-11-13: Brand-only nonformulary rules rest on the guide's own wording: "Brand name medications not listed in the medication list are not covered" (PDF p.2) and "Brand Name medications are covered only if they are included in the Closed Formulary list" (PDF p.3); exception route: Coverage Exception Process, PDF p.12 (printed XI). The p.5 line "any medications not on the formulary ... are not covered" is overridden for generics by "All generic medications are covered unless specifically excluded by your plan" (PDF p.3), so no generic is recorded as nonformulary from absence.]
